title: Binary Gap
description: Given a positive integer `n`, find and return the longest distance between any two adjacent `1`s in the binary representation of `n`. Two `1`s are adjacent if there are only `0`s separating them (possibly none). The distance between two `1`s is the absolute difference between their bit positions. If there are fewer than two `1`s, return `0`.
hints: Scan bits from least significant to most significant while maintaining the index `last` of the most recently seen `1` bit.
Whenever you encounter a new `1` at bit index `pos`, update the answer with `pos - last` if `last != -1`.

examples.explanation: 22 in binary is 10110; adjacent 1s are at distances 2 and 1, so the maximum is 2.
8 in binary is 1000, which contains only one 1 bit, so return 0.
5 in binary is 101; the two 1 bits are separated by distance 2.
